certificate: ✓ NS-4 rider cancelled more than 3 min after matching [case] 400 s after acceptance (F4)

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The trip was a RydeX (non-taxi) instant booking cancelled by the rider 6 min 40 s after acceptance (08:40:00 → 08:46:40), so the only route to a $6.61 cancellation fee is NS-0's 'cancelled_by = rider' branch, which sends the case to NS-4.

Under NS-4 the fee turns on the 3-minute matching clock, not on whether the driver had arrived: the rider cancelled at 6 min 40 s after matching (F4, F8), which is past the ≤ 3:00 free-cancellation window, so the $6.61 charge is prima facie valid on the timestamps alone.

The driver did not actually qualify for the fee under Ryde's own arrival standards: the driver's own arrival message came at 08:42 (F10) while he only entered the 200 m pickup zone at 08:41:35 and was still 41 m away and stationary until the rider cancelled (F2, F3), and the record of the 'I'm Here' tap is internally inconsistent (F6 versus F7), leaving the driver-side arrival condition unproven.

Because NS-4 admits no free-cancellation excuse for a driver not yet at the pickup point (no ETA-based waiver exists), the rider's only remedy for this $6.61 is a fee-waiver/refund request, which NS-7 expressly contemplates and which is not time-barred here — the request is made well within 30 days of the trip.

The rider has no history of upheld no-show or route disputes (0 upheld on either basis in 90 days), so this cancellation is not a pattern of abuse and Ryde's discretionary waiver under NS-7 should be exercised in her favour.

The driver, by contrast, carries 2 disputes with 1 upheld (no-show) in the last 90 days and 699 trips in the same window (F17), which is relevant context for how the arrival-record inconsistency in F6/F7 should be weighted, though it cannot itself decide this case.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled 6 min 40 s after acceptance (F4, F8), which is beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window in NS-4 — this is the single strongest fact against us and the driver will lead with it.

NS-4 states in terms that the driver's not having arrived is not a ground for free cancellation; the rider's own complaint ('the driver had not even arrived') therefore has no support in the policy as written (F10, F11 acknowledged).
The rider's own chat admits the real reason was a change of plans — 'Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel' (F11) — which shows the cancellation was voluntary rather than driven by driver conduct.

The system records show the driver was within 200 m of the pickup for a cumulative 5 min 5 s and stationary 41 m away (F2, F3), so an argument that the driver never turned up will not survive against the GPS record.
F6 records an 'I'm Here' tap at 08:42:15 39 m from the pickup, which if the panel resolves the F6/F7 inconsistency in the driver's favour would satisfy the driver-side arrival standard and defeat C3.

claims.assertion: This is a rider cancellation on an on-demand RydeX trip, cancelled 6 min 40 s after matching (accepted 08:40:00, cancelled by rider 08:46:40), i.e. well past the 3-minute mark, so the $6.61 cancellation fee stands under the rider-cancel branch.
The driver was on time and at the pickup: GPS shows the closest approach 39 m from the pickup at 08:42:40 and the first entry within 200 m at 08:41:35, 4 min 25 s before the rider cancelled.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 39 m from the pickup point and stayed within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap, satisfying the arrival/waiting elements that would support a no-show fee.

The driver waited stationary at the pickup for 4 min 40 s (08:42:00–08:46:40, 41 m away) and the app arrival was recorded at 08:41:35, so the cancellation came 5 min 5 s after recorded arrival — the rider was not left waiting and the driver did not lose time by his own fault.

The rider's own message at 08:45 states "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel", i.e. the cancellation cause is the rider's change of plans, not any driver delay or failure to arrive — which is exactly the risk allocation the cancellation fee covers.
The charged amount equals the published cancellation fee and no surge was applied ($6.61, multiplier 1.0×), so there is no overcharge to adjust.

Ryde's policy contains no free-cancellation rule based on driver lateness or ETA, so the rider's ground that "the driver had not even arrived" is not a basis to waive the fee; the system records show the driver had in fact arrived.

The rider filed within the 30-day window and the fee, if it were ever refunded, would be by voucher only; the driver's earned share of the $6.61 should not be disturbed by a complaint that rests solely on a change of plans.

weaknesses: The timeline slice contains contradictory entries on the "I'm Here" tap: F6 records a tap at 08:42:15, while F7 states driver_pressed_here_at is null. F7 undercuts claim D3 and, since the rider-cancel branch (NS-4) is what governs this case, the tap element is not needed anyway — the fee stands on F4 alone.

The rider will argue the driver stayed 39–41 m away (F1, F3) rather than at the exact pickup bay and sent only a chat message (F10), so the rider could not identify the car; the 200 m data-layer radius covers this but the rider will press it.
The driver's own 90-day record shows 1 upheld no-show dispute among 2 disputes (F17), which the rider may use to question reliability of the driver's arrival evidence (F6).
The driver's written statement (F12) is unsupported detail beyond the GPS record and loses to system records where they differ (F3), so it adds nothing on its own.

points.response: Conceded as to liability: the trip was a RydeX on-demand booking cancelled by the rider 6 min 40 s after matching (F4, F8), so NS-4's >3:00 branch applies and the fee is valid on the clock alone; the rider does not dispute that.

A 39 m closest approach does not establish waiting 'at the pick-up point' for a different purpose; more importantly the driver's own chat places him at the pickup only at 08:42 (F10) while GPS shows his first entry within 200 m at 08:41:35 (F2), and the timeline itself records the platform arrival at 08:41:35 (F5) — a record the driver cannot use to prove he arrived before he did.

F6 and F7 contradict each other on the 'I'm Here' tap, so the (i) element of NS-1 is unproven on the record; but D3 is beside the point — NS-1 concerns a driver-cancelled no-show, whereas here the rider cancelled (F4) and NS-4 governs.

The driver's stationary period ran 08:42:00–08:46:40 at 41 m away (F3), which shows he waited but also that he never closed the last 39–41 m or sent more than one identification-free message (F1, F10) — relevant to the equitable waiver under NS-7, not to the legal validity of the charge.
Conceded: the rider's own message 'Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel' (F11) is the cause of cancellation, so the rider's argument that the driver's non-arrival excuses the fee fails under NS-4.

Conceded: the charge equals the published $6.61 with no surge (F8, F9), so there is no FARE-1 overcharge component to adjust and the rider's request is limited to the discretionary fee waiver under NS-7.

The rider's original ground that the driver 'had not even arrived' is withdrawn — GPS shows he was within 200 m from 08:41:35 (F2) — so the rider rests solely on NS-7's fee-waiver avenue, which the driver's brief does not contest on the merits.

NS-7 vests the waiver discretion in Ryde and expressly permits a $6.61 voucher refund; the rider's clean 90-day record with 0 upheld no-show or route disputes in 90 days (F16) is the ground on which that discretion should be exercised, and the driver's counter-reliance on F17 (699 trips, 1 upheld no-show in 90 d) cuts both ways but cannot itself decide the case.

Accepted as framed: the case is a rider cancellation on a non-taxi instant booking and reaches the fee only through NS-0 → NS-4 (F4, F8). That route is where the driver wins, not where the rider does.

The rider's own framing defeats the complaint: a cancellation made beyond the 3-minute matching clock makes the $6.61 fee stand on the timestamps alone, and the rider here cancelled 6 min 40 s after matching (F4, F8), so the fee is valid without any driver-side element.

The arrival standards in NS-1 speak to the driver's $6.61/$4.50 entitlement assumption against a rider who does not appear and are irrelevant to a rider-initiated cancellation under NS-4; in any event the GPS record shows the driver first within 200 m at 08:41:35, stationary 41 m from the pickup for 4 min 40 s, and never having tapped nothing — F6 (tap 08:42:15, 39 m) is corroborated by the rider's own admission of the driver's arrival message (F10, F11).

Ryde's policy contains no ETA or lateness-based free-cancellation rule, and NS-4 expressly states the driver's not having arrived is not a ground for free cancellation; the rider's own conduct — cancelling because 'plans changed' (F11) — is a voluntary cancellation, not a fee-waiver ground, and NS-7's 30-day window merely fixes timing, it does not create a waiver entitlement.

The rider's clean 90-day record (F16) cannot manufacture a waiver where NS-4 sets a bright-line 3-minute rule and the system records put the cancellation at 6 min 40 s with the driver already at the pickup (F4, F5, F1); Ryde's fee suspension discretion is not a rider entitlement under any numbered clause.

The rider's own case establishes the 1 upheld no-show dispute in the driver's 90-day record is only the one the rider is now contesting, and profile facts cannot decide this case; the GPS arrival record (F2, F3, F5) independently establishes the driver was at the pickup.
